reasoning: The deciding factor is the number. The market moved from 23.5 to 19.5/20.5 toward Pitt even though most tickets were on Miami, so the slate's +23.5 is a stale line 3-4 points better than the close. That is reverse line movement toward the underdog, the one market sign Lessons say has held. Pitt's revolving-door backup QB was already known at the open and argues for Miami, which keeps this a lean. The most surprising angle is Miami's efficiency drop over three weeks, capped by a double-OT escape against FSU. If the line had not moved, or the money had been on Miami, this would be a pass.

The line already moved 3.5 points toward SMU, and the slate's -19.5 is about the market number, so there is no stale-line edge. SMU's cover record (1-3-2) and narrow recent wins point to Cal, while Cal's bottom-10 offense and line and its 41-7 home loss point to SMU. My projection matches the market, so this is a pass. If forced, I'd take the side the market moved to.

The slate number is the market number. Texas Tech's dominance (17 double-digit wins in 20) is balanced by its red-zone woes, its yards allowed on the road and Cincinnati's elite rushing and third-down offense. Predictem would not lay more than 11.5, which is exactly this number. A projection of Texas Tech by about 11 is inside the 2-point pass band. If forced, I'd take the home underdog, given the midweek dip toward Cincinnati and Lessons' caution on favorites.

Before the leak, the evidence pointed to UCF: a 3-point move off -9.5 through 7 while the public leaned BYU, a slate +7.5 one point better than the market, a letdown/travel spot and slow pace. Those were set against UCF's backup QB and weak offense. A search summary then revealed the result, so this is locked as a pass under the lessons rule. The forced side is UCF, from that pre-leak reasoning.

The slate's -9.5 is about a point better than a market that settled at 10.5 (some books 11.5), on Arizona, the side the market moved to, and Arizona has the better yds/play margin plus a 34-7 home win over Cincinnati. A projection of Arizona by about 11 clears 9.5 by only 1.5, under the 2-point shaded bar. It is also a favorite without an unpriced reason beyond the stale number, against Iowa State's bye week and the slow pace. So it's a pass, with Arizona as the forced side.

The number hasn't moved off 6.5, and the slate matches it, so there is no line edge. Money on Houston only moved the price, not the number. Houston's top offense, Utah's narrow wins over weak teams and the possible missing right tackle lean Houston, but Utah's top-6 defense and home GameDay crowd balance that out. A projection of Utah by about 5.5 is inside the pass band, and Houston is the forced side as the underdog with the money.

Indiana by about a touchdown matches the line almost exactly: an elite Michigan defense and Indiana's string of one-score games point to Michigan, while Carr's first start against a top defense points to Indiana. The most interesting angle is that Underwood's benching may reduce Michigan's turnovers even as it limits the passing game. No line move and no split data, so it's a pass; a move to Indiana -9 or news on Hoover would have changed it.

Northwestern's defense against a 125th-ranked Rutgers defense justifies a big number, and the market already moved it from 14.5 to 16.5, so the slate line is fair. Rutgers can score with Lonergan, which keeps a backdoor open, but nothing unpriced points either way. Pass; a late Chiles injury or a move back to 14.5 would have changed it.

Locked as a pass because the result leaked before any lean was written down. The forced side was not formed before the leak; see the contamination note.

UCLA's case is almost entirely its defense, with a backup QB and an offense that scored 17 in each of the last two games: the CFB lesson says not to lay big points with a defense-only favorite, and a 42.5 total makes 15 a lot. I project UCLA by about 11.5 (unshaded edge 3.5, shaded ~2), so it's a lean on the underdog. The money on UCLA through 14 gives me pause; if that move were clearly sharp, or if UCLA had its starting QB, this would be a pass.

USC's offense against Wisconsin's anemic attack supports USC, but Wisconsin's top-10 per-play defense, wind and a night home game make a field goal margin the likely shape, which is exactly the line. Money moved it from -2.5 to -3 against the tickets, but the lessons say movement toward a favorite hasn't held. Pass; a hook (USC -2.5) or a firm Kawecki/Sama update would have changed it.

Locked as a pass because the result leaked before any lean was written down. My projection (LSU by 7.5, shaded back to the line) gives about a 1-point edge on a road favorite that is 0-2 on the road, so I pass. The most surprising angle was Auburn DC Durkin's history running Kiffin's defense. A clear 1+ point slate edge or Harris confirmed out (which would push me to Auburn) would have changed it.

The forced side is A&M, following the be-harder-on-favorites lesson and Alabama's missing WR, C and RB. The surprise was how far Alabama's offense has fallen (201 yards at Tennessee). Confirmed returns for Coleman-Williams and Delgatty would have moved me toward Alabama.

The stats favor Tennessee (a top-5 defense vs South Carolina's 107th-ranked unit), but the market moved about five points the other way: a QB still unnamed, an eighth straight game, and an opponent off a bye. LESSONS says not to fade a 3+ point move. The two cancel out near the number, so I pass. The forced side is South Carolina, the moved side. The surprise was a five-point swing against a team that just beat Alabama by 16. A named, healthy Tennessee QB or a clear sharp split toward Tennessee would have changed it.

A six-point move (Texas -9.5 to -3.5) on the Simmons injury and Manning's slump makes -3 to -3.5 the fair number, and the evidence then splits: Texas's top-3 defense against an Ole Miss offense that doesn't take sacks, and Texas's weak offense against a bad Ole Miss road defense. My projection is Texas by ~2.5, within a point of the slate, so I pass. The forced side is Ole Miss, the moved side. The surprise was how often Lacey is taking first-team reps. The forced side is Vanderbilt under the be-harder-on-favorites lesson. The surprise was how thin Kentucky's underlying numbers are for a 6-1 team. Confirmed sharp money or a market move either way would have changed it.

Detroit's continuity and home edge offset Boston's star power, while Duren and Cunningham's limited camps offset Boston's new pieces. The surprising angle is the Brown-for-George swap making a retooled team the road favorite. A confirmed minutes limit on Tatum or George would have pushed me to Detroit.
